prompts.text: Which family greeting always makes you feel at home?
Tell us about the relative who first taught you to cook something on your own.
An unplanned afternoon chatting in the kitchen or a planned family game night?
We find a box of family photographs without names on them. Who would you ask to help identify everyone?
Different generations often use the same nickname for entirely different reasons.
Remembering the names of people important to a relative is a quiet form of respect.
What's an expression an older family member uses that deserves an explanation?
Recall a family visit when the journey became more memorable than the occasion.
A cousin visits our home for the first time. What would help them settle in?
Who in the family tells the funniest stories about ordinary events?
What was the first household responsibility you felt proud to handle?
Make breakfast together or organise the evening meal as a team?
Tell us about a chore you disliked as a child but understand better now.
Families develop routines so gradually that nobody remembers who started them.
Two relatives prefer opposite approaches to keeping a shared room tidy. What would be a fair compromise?
A clear plan for chores avoids more tension than repeated reminders.
Which household task do you prefer doing quietly on your own?
Describe a small repair someone in the family showed you how to make.
Everyone arrives home tired and dinner still needs preparing. How should we divide the work?
Wash dishes together while talking or take turns doing them alone?
Which family meal brings back a particular memory for you?
Tell us about a recipe someone adapted when an ingredient was unavailable.
Bring back a favourite meal from childhood or try a new dish together?
We have one evening to prepare food for visiting relatives. Which dishes should take priority?
The stories behind meals often differ from the recipes themselves.
A simple meal where everyone feels welcome beats an elaborate menu with an exhausted host.
Who taught you how to choose good ingredients at a market?
Recall a celebration where something went wrong with the food but everyone enjoyed themselves.
A younger family member wants to learn a traditional dish. Who should guide the first attempt?
Which family food tradition would you like future generations to understand?
What's a childhood game you would still enjoy playing with the family?
Board games at home or a casual walk around the neighbourhood?
Tell us about the first time you beat an older relative at a game.
Family games often come with rules that outsiders have never heard of.
A game gets too competitive for one person. How would you make it enjoyable again?
Letting younger people choose a family activity occasionally teaches everyone something new.
Which relative always knows how to make a gathering lively?
Describe a family outing that became funny because nobody agreed on the route.
It's raining on the day of a planned outdoor gathering. What indoor activity would you suggest?
A friendly quiz about our family history or a group storytelling session?
What is one family celebration you look forward to each year?
Tell us about a birthday someone made meaningful without spending much.
A small gathering at home or a picnic in a familiar place?
Two family members share the same birthday and want different celebrations. How should we plan?
The traditions people remember most are not always the ones that cost the most.
Giving everyone a role in a celebration matters more than making every detail perfect.
Which family song reminds you of a wedding or holiday?
Recall a festive visit when somebody surprised you by joining in.
We're planning a reunion across different ages. What would keep children and adults comfortable?
What would you change about how we organise family celebrations?
Who in the family taught you a skill you still use?
Ask an elder to share a life story or learn a practical skill from them?
Tell us about advice you understood years after you first heard it.
The same family story sometimes changes depending on who remembers it.
An older relative wants to pass on a skill but nobody has much time. How should we organise a lesson?
Listening carefully to someone's story shows greater interest than finishing their sentences.
Which family saying do you agree with more as you grow older?
Describe a time a younger relative surprised you with a thoughtful point of view.
A teenager wants to explain a new interest the adults don't understand. How should we make room for it?
Record an elder telling a story or write the story together in a notebook?
Which part of family life makes you feel most supported?
Tell us about a difficult week when a relative helped in an unexpected way.
A practical favour during a busy day or a thoughtful check-in afterwards?
Someone is having a tough time but doesn't want to discuss it at dinner. How should we respect their space?
People offer comfort differently, even when they belong to the same family.
Asking someone what kind of help they want is better than assuming.
What helps you relax after a demanding family gathering?
Recall an occasion when a relative apologised in a way you appreciated.
Two people remember a disagreement differently. How would you encourage a calm conversation?
What is a gentle way to tell a relative you need more personal space?
Which family value matters most to you in everyday decisions?
Talk about a big decision around the table or have smaller conversations first?
Describe a choice an older family member made that you later came to appreciate.
Relatives often share a value but disagree over the best way to practise it.
We need to choose between two family commitments happening on the same day. What should guide us?
Showing up consistently matters more than making impressive promises.
How has your understanding of family responsibility changed as you've grown?
Tell us about a family decision that required patience from everyone.
A relative wants to change a long-standing tradition. How should the family hear their reasons?
Keep an old tradition unchanged or let every generation add something small?
Which place from your childhood would you like the family to visit together?
Describe a journey with relatives where you learnt something new about them.
A day trip to somewhere familiar or a short visit to an unfamiliar town?
We have a free Saturday and everyone wants a different outing. How should we choose?
A family outing sometimes reveals interests that rarely come up at home.
Good company makes a modest outing worth remembering.
What is one local place you would enjoy showing a younger relative?
Tell us about the first time you travelled without your parents or guardians.
An older relative tires quickly during a group excursion. How would you adjust the plan?
Which family trip would you happily repeat, and what made it work?
What would you like younger relatives to remember about spending time with you?
Keep a family photo album or collect written stories from different relatives?
Tell us about a conversation with a relative you wish you had recorded.
Small moments of attention sometimes become the memories people hold longest.
We're putting together a family keepsake with one contribution from everyone. What would you add?
Family closeness grows from regular contact rather than only major celebrations.
Which family habit do you hope continues ten years from now?
Describe a time the family welcomed someone new and helped them feel included.
Someone in the family moves far away. What simple routine would help us stay connected?
A monthly family call or occasional handwritten notes between relatives?
